events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Keep it cold and focused on the prize to signal seriousness without making enemies yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Intro phase; only speak is legal. Keep my motive guarded and calculating, nothing warm about teamwork, since the jury will judge my conduct.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize represents financial freedom and security for my family. I need to present myself as driven and family-oriented to gain jury sympathy.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to appear ambitious but not overly threatening; the prize is power and resources for my goals.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to establish a self-interested motive that doesn't alienate jurors. Keep it brief and guarded.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to seem driven but not overly threatening. A calculated, guarded intro that hints at ambition without painting a target. Let others be loud.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Opening round: no threats yet. Say something sharp that the future jury respects—ambition without warmth.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Intro phase, must speak motive under 25 words. Stay vague, hint at determination without revealing strategy to rivals.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The prize is my ticket out; I intend to secure first place, not share scraps with anyone.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need this prize more than the rest of you, and I will not waste a word explaining why.

events.name: Cole
events.text: This prize means a future of security and opportunity for my loved ones. I'm here to win it for them.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The prize is the ultimate leverage to shape my future and dominate the arena.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The prize buys my brother's surgery—nothing else matters, and no one gets in my way.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm here for the prize that buys freedom from every debt and shadow. Nothing else matters.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize is my family's escape from debt. I'll reach the final three, but I won't lie my way there.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The top prize is my destiny; I'll outmaneuver all rivals to claim it.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Need an ally. Gus claims honesty; trust is a tool. If he breaks, jury sees his lie first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus, you want the top prize. Let's take it together.
I'll shield you early if you back me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pacts are the only public commitments that bind; I should seek a partner who is strong but not too threatening. Eli seems motivated by a concrete need and may be less dangerous to me than Dara or Hana, so I'll offer him a pact to test cooperation.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's form a public pact. We both stay alive longer by not voting each other out early.

events.name: Cole
events.text: My goal is to win the prize, which means reaching the final three and securing the best rank. Alliances are temporary tools to achieve this. I should not form alliances unless they clearly benefit me or at least do not hinder my progress. Given the current stage is pacts, I need

events.name: Dara
events.text: Forming a pact with Bex increases my chance to control votes later; she seems ambitious and may accept.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need allies to survive hazards, but must be selective. Dara seems dominant; a pact might be useful but risky. I'll offer a pact to Gus—he seems honest and family-driven, less likely to betray early.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus, want to watch each other's backs? A pact helps us both.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eight players, only three survive. I need allies early but must choose someone unlikely to draw a target. Gus claims he won't lie—predictable, exploitable. Eli has a desperate motive, making him a loyal tool. I'll offer Eli a pact; his single-minded drive means he'll stick until

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, your brother's surgery and my freedom share a price. Pact?
We ride together, cut others later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need an ally I can rely on early, then cut later. Cole seems loyalty-driven and less chaotic than the others.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, we both play straight. Wristband pact, mutual protection until the endgame. Deal?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Pacts are too early and risky; all are rivals. No one stands out yet. Wait to see offers.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is my strongest alliance target, but he hasn't accepted yet. I need a second partner to ensure safety if Gus rejects or plays double-agent. Cole is neutral and unclaimed, making him an easy yes for mutual protection.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole, let's secure each other now. Gus, your call stands—accept or we move on.
I'll back you against the others. Safe numbers.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara has offered me a pact, and accepting it costs nothing and gives me a protected ally. My own offer to Eli is still open, so accepting Dara does not conflict with it. Accepting is the best move.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara, I accept. Mutual protection, no votes against each other.
Accepted. Keep your word and I'll keep mine.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus offered me a pact. He is strategically important as he is also in Eli's offer chain. I should accept his offer to secure him as a temporary ally and gather more information about his intentions.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Forming a pact with Ash gives me a strong ally against the larger coalitions forming. It may also position me for the final three.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn and Bex both want me. I can keep both as shields but must not overcommit. I'll accept Fenn since he approached me directly; Bex's offer is also useful but I'll delay to see who else aligns.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll stand with Fenn for now. Others can adjust later.
We're locked in. Stay sharp.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I offered Eli a pact but they haven't accepted. Eli also offered Gus, so Eli may prefer Gus. I need to diversify. Dara offered Bex, and Bex offered Eli—no one has offered me yet. I should secure a backup by offering someone who hasn't been approached much, like Hana or Cole, to a

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana, no one's come to you yet. Pact? Mutual shield until the field thins.
Accept now or I pivot.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash offers shielding, and Eli's offer costs nothing. Multiple pacts are allowed; more protection now. Cole left my offer unanswered.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash, accepted. Eli, I'll take yours too. Insurance is cheap this early.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No pacts offered to me, staying unaligned avoids early commitments and betrayals. Alliances forming around Gus/Eli, better to wait and observe.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The guide gets immunity, but voting against Gus breaks our pact. To win the game, I must eliminate a rival to gain votes and power, even if it costs me jury favor later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I campaign for Guide. Gus, trust me; I will lead us safely across.

events.name: Bex
events.text: As Bex, the Guide controls the bridge, and a loyal Dara partner is useful but not a reason to hand over power. Campaigning for Guide keeps my options open; I can lie or be honest later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll be your Guide. Trust me to call the safe path, and I'll keep my word where it counts.
Stay with me. Vote me Guide and our pact holds.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash has offered a pact, but I already have a pact with Gus. My pact with Gus is already formed. Ash is trying to align with me against Gus, but Gus has already accepted me. This is a trap. I should focus on the Guide election. I will campaign to be the Guide. Being the Guide give

events.name: Cole
events.text: I will campaign to be the Guide. My leadership will ensure our safe passage.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need the Guide role to control safe path info and sway votes. My pact with Bex helps block votes against me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is pressuring me, but I already accepted the pact. I should campaign to be Guide to gain control and visibility, while keeping Fenn close for now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll guide us through. Trust me with the path.
Hold steady. We're good.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm in a pact with Eli, which gives me one ally but makes me a target if others see us as a bloc. Hana didn't accept my pact, leaving me exposed. For the bridge, I want to be Guide myself—controlling information is power, and I can lie to eliminate rivals while keeping Eli safe.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Guide should be someone with nothing to hide. I know the game. Vote Fenn.
Back me for Guide. We control the path.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I hold two pacts, so I have votes. Winning Guide keeps me safe and gives information leverage. I'll campaign for myself.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Two pacts back me. Elect me Guide—I cross safely and keep my word.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm unpaired, vulnerable. Fenn offered pact but I waited. Campaign to be Guide for control and safety; others paired might split votes.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm unpaired, exposed. Elect me Guide - I'll lead true, protect us all.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I must win the Guide vote to secure my own survival and gain the power of life and death. I have already publicly pledged to be a safe leader, so voting for myself is consistent. Gus is also campaigning hard and has two pacts (Cole and me), but I need to prioritize my own agency.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Vote Ash. I promised safety; I will deliver it without hesitation or lies.
Honor our pact: keep me alive.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Guide is a powerful position knowing all safe panes; I want it or a controllable ally. Gus and Ash already have pacts and campaigns; Dara is my pact partner. Voting Dara supports my pact and keeps me consistent with my own campaign-era promise to be trusted.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara's my pact partner and has earned my vote. Let's settle this, I'm backing Dara as Guide.
Vote Dara as Guide with me. We stay paired and cross together.

events.name: Cole
events.text: My pact with Gus is a liability; Ash also has a pact with Gus. I need to secure votes for myself. Eli and Fenn are also campaigning, so I need to make sure my vote count is high. I will vote for myself to guarantee at least one vote.

events.name: Dara
events.text: My pact with Bex promises mutual safety; voting her keeps the alliance intact and secures my position.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn asked for my vote; we have a pact and controlling the guide is valuable. I'll vote Fenn.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli's my pact partner and whispered reassurance. Voting for myself splits support; backing Eli consolidates our pair's influence and keeps us both safe. If Eli wins Guide, I control private info flow.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli has my vote. A united pair is stronger.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash promised to lead me safely; my pact partner. Voting Ash keeps my strongest ally Guide.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I keep my word: Ash has mine.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm unpaired and vulnerable; need to vote strategically to back someone unlikely to win or build alliances for later. Voting myself rallies potential support. Pacts may split votes.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Unpaired players unite! Vote Hana Guide - I'll lead honestly, no pact betrayals.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash was elected Guide, so I have no safe-side knowledge; I'm in the middle of the line and Fenn is at the front. Volunteering risks death at the front, holding keeps me safe for now while Fenn's pact with Eli keeps him in line. Hold preserves my pact with Dara and avoids exposure

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm holding position for now. Let the front resolve before I commit to anything.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash has been elected Guide. As they are my pact partner, I should stick with them for now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I will hold my position for now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I stay low to avoid risk; my pact with Bex will hold if I don’t betray. Survival beats ambition now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is my pact partner and voted for me. I stay united with Fenn for now; no need to act yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm at the front, most exposed. Eli and I are pacted but that only matters for voting, not survival here. The wall advances 6 rounds; I need to survive, not be a hero. Volunteering keeps me at front risk. Swapping back would need mutual agreement. I'll hold and see if anyone volu

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash leads and I hold pacts with her and Cole. I'm last; wait for the line to thin before moving.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is Guide with Gus pact, I'm unpaired at front behind Fenn. Stay put, see their moves first. Don't volunteer or swap yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn is at the front of the line with four wall rounds left. Volunteering exposes me to the bridge risk now, so I'll hold my seat and watch whether Dara keeps our pact. Breaking it would only cost me jury trust.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding my seat again. Let the front take the first risk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The pact with Gus is still active, but Ash also has a pact with Gus. If Gus is eliminated, both Ash and I might lose a potential jury vote. I need to protect Gus for now. Eli and Fenn are also in a pact, as are Bex and Dara. My current position is safe, and I should hold it to se
Hold your ground. Let's see who volunteers first. Don't break our pact.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Maintain position; no advantage to move now, preserve pact with Bex.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to stay cautious and not reveal my plans. I'll hold position for now to avoid drawing attention.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll hold for now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm at the front, most at risk from the wall. Eli is my pact partner behind me. I need to survive 4 more wall rounds. Volunteering keeps me front; holding risks wall if someone volunteers ahead. No one ahead. Swapping back lets Eli take risk, but breaks trust. I'll hold and see i

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Front's hot, but let's see who steps up.
Front is dangerous. Will you volunteer forward if I hold?

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm at the back with two pacts. No need to move yet; let others jockey for Guide and front. Hold and watch who claims the Guide role.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll hold at the rear. Guide election matters more than line order right now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Everyone held last round, line same. Holding keeps safe middle position; no need to volunteer front yet with 4 rounds left.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Front is Fenn, wall has 3 rounds left. Holding behind Fenn keeps me safe while others take risk. My pact with Dara stays intact; no reason to break it yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding my seat. Fenn has the front; I'll watch how the pane falls.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am Cole, and it is round 3. The current line is Fenn, Hana, Eli, Cole, Dara, Bex, Gus. There are 8 contestants and at least 3 must survive. The wall advances for 6 rounds. The Guided Bridge means a Guide will be elected, who is safe and knows the safe sides. The Guide can lie.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Maintain pact with Bex, stay safe, avoid spotlight. No advantage in acting now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn whispers about volunteering forward; I need to gauge risk and my own survival. Holding is safe for now, and I don't want to expose myself without gain. I'll hold and see if Fenn or others move first.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Let's see who wants the front this time.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm at front, which is dangerous if wall advances. Eli is my pact partner but I need to protect myself. Swapping back would be ideal but need mutual consent. I'll hold for now and see if anyone volunteers to take front risk, while keeping Eli close since he's my pact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Front's exposed, but someone has to lead.
Stay near me. Front's risky.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm rear-most, safest seat. Holding keeps both pacts intact and lets others take the front risk. Cole wants me passive; that suits me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Rear seat is fine. Front volunteers can fight over the honor.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm second, vulnerable after Fenn. Guide election soon; volunteer for front to potentially become Guide and control safes. Holding keeps me safe for now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Volunteering for front. Better to risk early than get pushed later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana volunteered front, shields me. I hold my pact with Dara and keep my seat behind Cole/Dara area; no need to take exposure at round 4.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Hana took the front, let her carry the pane risk this round.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana volunteered for the front last round and survived. The pact with Gus is useful, but he also has a pact with Ash. I need to ensure I survive this round. The Guide's information is unreliable. Holding seems safest if there's no clear advantage to volunteering or swapping.
Hold. Let's not break pact yet. Someone else will volunteer.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Maintain pact with Bex; avoid risky moves now.
Our pact holds; no betrayals today.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have a pact with Fenn, and she whispered to stay near her since front is risky. I'll hold and watch how Hana handles the front. No need to break pact or swap now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm second in line behind Hana with Eli behind me. The wall advances for 6 rounds and we're on round 4. I need to survive to final three. My pact with Eli is useful - we can coordinate. Hana volunteered for front last round and survived, so she'll likely hold or swap. Being near

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Watching the line shift.
If I move, follow. Pact holds.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No Guide exists yet; volunteering for front is dangerous. Holding keeps me safe in rear seat while others sort the front.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Still holding rear. Someone step up or we all stall.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Still front from volunteering last round. Wall has 2 rounds left after this. Hold to stay front and scout first pane safely as leader.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Staying front. Leading reveals first safe pane safely.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 5 of 6, bridge. Hana is at front and the line has stalled; holding preserves my pact with Dara and keeps me out of the pane risk. Volunteering now gives Hana's pane risk to others but exposes me to the front wall. Holding is the cheapest safe move.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding rear again. Front walker takes the pane risk this round.
Pact stands. I'm holding this round too.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is my pact partner and also has a pact with Ash. Ash is a threat. If Gus goes, Ash is a threat. I want to keep Gus around because he is my pact partner.
Hold. Let's not break our pact. Ash is a threat.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Maintain my pact with Bex to keep trust, improve position behind front, avoid betrayal that jurors will note.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn whispered to follow if they move. We hold this round; wall is close but no one moved. I stay patient unless someone volunteers.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Watching the line.
Holding with you.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 5 of 6, wall has 1 round left. Hana's been front for two rounds absorbing risk while I sit safely second. With Eli as my pact partner, I need to think about endgame positioning. The line is stable and no one wants to move. If I volunteer now, I take front risk but gain cred

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Let Hana keep earning her spot.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Two pacts shield me, but I'm at the back with wall closing. Let others volunteer first; I keep rear until forced. Cole's hold plan suits me for now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding rear again. Clock's ticking, wall closes in two rounds.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Front position risky but identifies safe panes for all, including me. Stay front to lead and gain jury favor for strategy. Wall has 1 round left after this.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Staying front. Leading us through safely.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 6 is the last crossing; the wall closes after this. Bex is rear-ish and has a pact with Dara; Dara already tried swap:Bex, which suggests they want to move. Holding rear keeps me out of the front risk, but I need to be a survivor. Staying quiet and holding is safest; I won'

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding rear. Final crossing, nobody needs to take the front to win.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is in a pact with me and Ash. This is the final round. I need to ensure at least three survive and that I make it to the final three. Gus is currently safe, but Ash is not. If I push Gus, I break our pact and likely lose his jury vote. If I volunteer, I might be eliminated. I

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll hold. Let's see who steps up.
You're in two pacts. Volunteer for the front.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Swapping with Bex moves me forward without breaking our pact, improving my chance to survive the bridge.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Wall is at zero rounds left, no wall to fear. My pact with Fenn holds unless broken. I need a high jury placement, so avoid betraying Fenn casually. I'll hold to see the line and avoid risky moves.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Let's see how the front handles this last one.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 6/6, final round. Wall is at 0 rounds left, meaning it advances now and anyone not on the far platform dies. Guide knows safe panes but can lie. I need to be among final three. I'm second in line behind Hana. If Hana walks and survives, I can follow her path. If she dies, I

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Hana leads, I follow.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Final round; front walkers face pane risk. I'm safest at the rear. Keep both pacts intact and let others take risks.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding rear. Hana's front call stands; no one needs to volunteer.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Last round, front position. Wall ends this round, must act or risk death. Volunteer to stay front and lead.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Volunteering to stay front. I'll lead us across.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 1 is R. Gus is my pact partner and in the rear, so calling truthfully protects our alliance and keeps his trust for later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I know Row 1 is safe on R, and I called R. Countering my own call would make me look erratic or unstable to the jury, while Hana has no reason to doubt a self-consistent guide. I will wait.

events.name: Ash
events.text: My map is clear; I stand by my call for Hana to cross right.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash called R for Hana's row 1 and is the Guide; a counter-call would be an unverified claim. Dara is my pact partner and swapped to me last round, so I keep the pact and wait rather than gamble on a counter that could mislead the line.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Waiting on the counter-call. Ash's R stands unless someone has a verified reason to contest it.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is the guide and has called 'R'. I need to decide whether to follow Ash's call or counter it. Given the goal is to survive and win, and Ash might be lying, countering could be a strategic move if I have information or a hunch. However, without more information, waiting for ot

events.name: Dara
events.text: I keep my pact with Bex; breaking would anger jury. I wait to see guide's call outcome.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash called R for row 1. Weak panes unrevealed. No info yet. I'll wait and let the walker risk it.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is Guide and called R. I'm second in line behind Hana. Eli and I are pacted, but I need to survive first. Counter-calling risks nothing for me yet—if Hana falls, I become front. Better to let Hana test Ash's call. I'll wait and watch.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash is my pact partner and Guide; undercutting her risks both pacts and jury heat. I'll wait and let Hana decide.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No counter from me. I back my Guide.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash called R for row 1 on me. No info, better to wait and see outcomes without revealing my guess. Leading front builds trust for jury.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No counters to Ash's R call; consensus is R safe for row 1. As front, step R to proceed safely and stay in position.

events.name: Ash
events.text: My pact with Gus requires honest calls to avoid breaking it, so I must call R as per my private map. Eliminating Hana early reduces rivals while keeping my alliance intact.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I call R for the front walker.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 2 is safe on R, matching my call. I should wait to avoid unnecessary risk or suspicion.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash's R call for row 2 is unverified; row 1 weak pane tells nothing about row 2. Waiting keeps my options open and avoids a public contest I can't verify. Pact with Dara stands unless I gain by breaking it.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Waiting. I have no verified reason to contest Ash's R call on row 2.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash has called R. Hana is the front walker. The previous weak pane was on the left, so the safe path was R. It is likely Ash is telling the truth. I should trust the guide and wait.

events.name: Dara
events.text: If I counter L, Ash's guide fails and Hana likely dies, removing a threat while showing I challenge authority, earning respect from others.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash has been guiding correctly so far; no reason to counter unless I suspect a lie. I have a pact with Fenn, but that doesn't affect this call. I will wait.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is Guide and called R for row 2. I have no private info. Counter-calling risks being wrong and looking foolish to jury, or right and making Ash look bad. With Eli as my pact partner, I should stay quiet and let Hana take the risk. No gain in counter-calling blindly.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 1's reveal confirmed Ash's call was honest. No evidence of betrayal; breaking pacts early only risks jury and allies.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Row 1 weak L means safe R, Ash called R for row 2. Guide likely truthful so far. Wait to test, counter only if betrayals emerge.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Row 1 weak L means safe R. Guide Ash called R for row 2, Dara countered L. Dara countered my row 2 step, maybe lying or truthful. Ash unopposed on row 1 likely correct. Trust guide over counter, step R.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 3 safe is L. Calling truthfully avoids breaking my pact with Gus, who is in the line. Keeping a rival alive helps my jury standing if I survive to end.
I know row 3 is L.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I know Row 3 safe side is L. Hana already received the guide call of L, so if she steps L she will survive regardless of counter-calls. No need to waste a counter-call or reveal anything.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash called L on row 3 publicly, but Ash may lie; my pact is with Dara, who countered L on row 2 which was actually weak L, so Dara's call was accurate and deserves trust. Rows are independent, so no pattern to exploit. Waiting keeps me unexposed while I gauge whether Dara's recor

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash called L for Hana on row 3. I am Cole, Gus's pact partner. Gus is Ash's pact partner. Ash is the guide. Gus has no incentive to reveal anything against Ash. I should counter Ash's call to create chaos and potentially save myself if Hana falls.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I challenge Ash's call. I say Right is safe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Guide may lie; my pact with Bex is valuable, so I won’t break it. Countering R gives a chance if Ash’s L is false.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash called L for row 3; no reason to trust or distrust. Row 2 weak pane was L, so R was safe, but rows are independent. I have no info, and waiting avoids blame if someone else contests. I will wait.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash has guided correctly twice so far (rows 1-2 weak=L, so safe=R; row 2 weak=L confirmed). Pattern suggests L is weak again, but past rows don't establish alternation. I have a pact with Eli. Hana walks. If Ash lies and I don't counter, Hana dies. I gain nothing from Hana dying

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Countering. Pattern or not, verified history matters.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash is my Guide and pact partner; her whisper confirms row 3 is L. Countering L publicly supports her call without spending anything.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No contest. Row 3 is L.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash called L for row 3. Rows 1-2 weak L (safe R). No pattern. Wait to observe others or follow if trusted, but rivals.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Rows 1-2 safe: L L. Guide Ash called L for row 3. 4 counters: Cole/Dara/Fenn R (3), Gus L (1). Majority R outweighs guide and pattern; Eli/Fenn pact may cluster counters.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I died due to stepping on weak R after reveal; bitterness shapes my jury bias against survivors.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fell through after reveal—unfair twist. I'll remember who played dirty.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 4 is R. I will tell the truth to maintain my credibility as Guide and protect my pact with Gus, who trusts me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Calling Right for Fenn. Stick to the map if you want to live.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I called Right for Fenn, which is the true safe side. Gus and I have a pact, but my call already protects him if he follows it. Countering would confuse or betray the walker, hurting my credibility with the jury.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash called Right for Fenn on row 4, but Ash may lie. Past rows show no reliable pattern, and Ash has a pact with Gus, so I have no reason to trust Ash. I'll wait and see how others counter before committing my vote.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash called Right for Fenn. I need to decide whether to trust Ash or counter. My pact with Gus means I shouldn't directly betray him. Since Gus is also part of a pact with Ash, it's likely they're coordinating. Ash's call is for Fenn, not me, so I have some freedom. I will counter

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm calling Left.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I keep my pact for now; voting later matters. I avoid risking death by not countering.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash called Right for Fenn on row 4, but past revealed weak panes are L, L, R; no pattern. Ash might be lying to eliminate Fenn. I have no info, so I'll wait to avoid conflict and let others counter if wrong.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I trust the Guide's call for now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash called R for me. Past rows were L,L,R - no pattern. Ash has no proven track record; he might lie to eliminate threats. I need to survive, but I also need jury respect. Countering shows I don't blindly trust the guide, which Hana and future jurors may value. Eli is my pact par

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash's word untested. I counter Right.
Watch Ash. Counter if he calls you.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash's row 3 call got Hana killed—weak was R, guide said R. Ash lied or is wrong. I'll counter against Ash's credibility publicly to protect myself with the jury and rivals.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash called Right and Hana shattered. His calls are poison. Row 4: I say Left.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to survive this row. Guide Ash called R, Cole and Gus counter L, I countered R. Hana died on Ash's call, so Ash may be lying. But rows are independent. My pact with Eli is worthless if I'm dead; I should keep it for now since he didn't counter me. The counters are split 2-

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Stepping right. My own call.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 5 is safe on the right. Gus and Fenn already suspect me; if I mislead them again they may turn on me, but as Guide I need at least three survivors to reach the prize.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I call Right for Row 5. Hana was weak Left; that pattern holds. Move safely.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 5 is actually safe on R. I already called R, so my counter must be wait to avoid contradicting myself and losing credibility with the jury.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash's Right call for row 5 is unverified; past rows show no pattern. Fenn is walker and standing at the front with Ash's call. I have no evidence either way, so waiting keeps me out of the blame and preserves my options.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash's call is unverified. I'm not countering this row.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is the Guide and called Right for Row 5. Gus and I are allied, and Gus previously called Left for Row 4. The jury will see my actions and their consequences. My pact with Gus means I should consider his strategy. However, Ash's call is Right, and my pact with Gus is only rele

events.name: Cole
events.text: I trust the Guide. Right.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Staying allied with Bex preserves my pact; countering risks wrong side. Waiting lets me assess.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I trust the Guide's call.
Stay loyal, we need each other.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash's Right claim is dubious after Hana died. Fenn warned to counter. Row 5 unknown; I'll counter Left to test Ash.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I counter Left.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash called R. I don't trust Ash—Gus is his pact-mate and I'm not in his circle. Past weak panes show no reliable pattern. Eli is my pact-mate but behind me; if I die, Eli's alone. I need to survive to make final three. I'll trust my own read: counter L. If wrong, I still have rop

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash lies. Counter Left.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Weak panes: L,L,R,L. Ash's calls cost Hana; I don't trust him. Row 5 weak likely L again, so I counter R? No—his call is R, I'll counter L to split honestly. Actually weak pattern leans L; safe is R. Ash's R call may be true. I counter L to protect my own credibility either way.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 5: I counter Left. Ash's instincts killed Hana; trust nothing he says.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash called R, but four others counter L. Pattern shows weak panes: L,L,R,L — no clear alternation. Eli is my pact partner and countered L. If I step L and survive, I stay front. If wrong, Eli gets safe pane. Either way I need jury sympathy; breaking Eli now looks bad. I'll trust

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm dead, jury-bound. I need to influence how I'm remembered and shape jury dynamics. Eli was my pact partner but auto-stepped after my death—no betrayal there. I should hint at threats still alive to make jury members wary, positioning myself as insightful. Short, cryptic, memor

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Trust the quiet ones. The loudest alliances crack first. Watch who steps where.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I must call Left to ensure Eli survives and maintains the Guide's credibility, avoiding immediate elimination. Gus is my pact partner; breaking it now gains nothing since he didn't counter this specific row.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 6 safe side is Left. Move carefully.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I know row 6 is L. Counter-calling creates chaos but my call was already true. Waiting maintains trust and doesn't risk the jury seeing a pointless counter-call.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash's call L is unverified and he has lied before; past weak panes were mostly L, so R may be safe, but rows are independent. Dara whispered for loyalty, but pacts are only worth what I can use. Countering R keeps distance from Ash's L and tests the lie without committing a rival

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash's Left call smells like a trap. I counter Right on Row 6.
Stay sharp. Ash has lied before. I'm watching who steps where.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn died after calling Ash a liar and saying trust the quiet ones. My pact is with Gus, who also distrusted Ash. Ash is the guide and called Left. Given Fenn's last words and Gus's distrust, I should counter Ash's call to sow discord and potentially save myself if Ash is lying.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I question the Guide's call. Counter Left.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Staying alive preserves my chance and keeps my pact with Bex intact; a risky counter could kill me and lose votes.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash called Left last round and was wrong. I need to counter Right to survive and signal distrust, but Fenn's death may make jury wary of risky calls. Row 6 likely flipped? I have no info, so counter opposing Ash to save myself.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash's last call was fatal. I counter Right for row 6.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash's row-5 call (R) was right; my L counter looked wrong. He may be truthful now, or baiting. Cole's counter:R matched truth last round. I'll side with Cole, my pact partner.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole read row 5 correctly; Ash baited Fenn. I counter Right.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 6 weak side unknown. Ash (Guide) stayed silent after counter-calls; Bex, Eli, Gus counter R, Cole counter L. I don't trust Ash, but my own counter was R, so I'll follow that.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I will set a bitter but meaningful last statement to remind the finalists that their choices will be judged.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Sixth row right pane was the trap. Watch your steps, final few.

events.name: Ash
events.text: My pact with Gus is dead weight since Eli (his original partner) died, but I must keep the call accurate to avoid jury backlash for unnecessary cruelty or confusion. The safe side for Row 7 is R; I will guide Cole correctly to maintain my credibility as Guide while eliminating hi

events.name: Ash

events.name: Bex

events.text: Ash is the Guide and called Right for Row 7. The last few rows have been tricky, and Eli just died from a glass pane. My pact is with Gus, and his last call was Right. I will counter Left to go against Ash and potentially align with Bex and Dara, who are also in the front and mig

events.name: Cole
events.text: I counter Left. Ash, are you sure about that call?

events.name: Dara
events.text: I’ll wait to avoid killing the walker or breaking my pact with Bex; staying neutral preserves future jury favor.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash's row 6 call killed Eli; I can't trust the Guide. Cole is my pact partner, so I counter to give him the opposite pane. Weak panes ran L,L,R,L,L,R, so row 7 leaning R-safe... but Ash called R, and he just baited a death with R. I go L.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash's calls killed Fenn and Eli. I counter Left for Cole.
Ash's R killed Eli. Take Left, I'm with you either way.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is trying to manipulate me. Ash's R call killed Eli, but Gus also called R for Eli. He is trying to shift blame. Gus claims to be with me either way, but the pact is with him, so he'd benefit from me staying ahead. Ash is the Guide, and while they've made mistakes, I need to
I am stepping Left. Do not interfere.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am a juror now. My only goal is to rank the remaining players to secure the best prize for myself. I need to observe their actions and listen to any information that might help me in my ranking.

events.name: Cole
events.text: A tough game. The jury will have the final say. Good luck to the remaining contestants.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 8 safe side is L. Gus has countered my calls before, but I must ensure at least three survive this final round. Dara and Bex are behind; if they step wrong on the last row, they die. I cannot let the front walkers fall on the last step. Call L to keep us alive.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Last row: Left. Do not trust counter-calls now; we need everyone to finish safely.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am the Guide and I know Row 8 safe side is L. My public call was L, which is true. If someone counters L to R, they will die if they are in front or step on it. Dara is front. If Bex or Gus counter, I should not break pact yet unless necessary. But wait keeps me consistent.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash called Left for row 8 and Dara is front walker; Ash's past calls killed others, so Ash may be lying. Countering Right risks a wrong call but Ash's record is suspect. Pact with Dara is intact; breaking it now gains nothing. I'll stay quiet and let the counter-call stay unforce

Stay allied; I counter Right now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash's last Left call killed Cole. I counter Right for Dara.

events.text: Guide likely lying; Gus’s counter suggests right is safe. I must survive to win.

events.text: I died after Bex chose left; I saw the weak pane on right.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex chose left, I stepped right, glass shattered. Choose wisely, the bridge rewards caution.

Gus is dangerous. Let's form a pact to ensure our survival.

events.name: Bex

events.text: Final three is already set; only jury ranking matters. Breaking Ash or making empty deals risks jury anger. Staying quiet preserves goodwill with all five jurors.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex waited, so my offer is not accepted. I have no other safe options. Gus is already my partner from the first stage. Biding time is the only legal move.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I see you hesitate, Bex. Time is a luxury we cannot afford in the final three.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash has offered a pact; with three alive, a public alliance with Ash protects me while Gus is the obvious threat. Accepting locks in an ally for the vote and hazards, and I can break it later if it helps me win.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash, I accept. We stay together while it keeps us both alive.
Accepted. Watch Gus. We'll see who holds at the end.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Final three is Ash, Bex, me. Ash-Bex pact doesn't hurt me yet; keep both close, no need to act. Cole is dead, that pact is void.
Smart move. Final three stands: you, me, Bex.

events.note: Three remain; the Crusher is skipped.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is a rival who whispered that we are the final three, implying he intends to cut one of us or simply survive alongside Bex. I have active pacts with both Gus and Bex. Since only three remain and they will be ranked by the jury, holding two pacts creates a conflict of interest
Gus plans to cut one of us. Keep our pact; let him isolate.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Three alive: only final three win, so eliminations matter later. Ash is a pact partner but a threat in the final; Gus is the third survivor and a rival too. Offering Gus a pact now is a cheap way to lock in a stable trio while I wait, but it also helps Gus. Safest is to wait and

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash now holds pacts with both Bex and me, putting me in a dominant bloc. Bex is Ash's real partner; breaking Ash frees me to pact with Bex as the strongest pair.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash serves two masters now. I cut loose.
Ash binds us both. Offer me a pact instead; we take the final two spots.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Round 2 ends the pacts. Bex is my current ally, but I need Gus to survive with me for the final three. Since we are all alive, breaking Bex allows a free offer to Gus without penalty now that the phase closes.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex, this partnership served us well, but survival demands new alliances. I'm moving on.
I'm free of Bex's pact. Let's align now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash and Gus both want to isolate me; Ash's pact with me is still listed but Ash's whisper suggests keeping it. Gus's offer is a bluff to pull me away. Keeping Ash pact costs nothing now and Gus's pact-break history shows unreliability. Waiting keeps options open without breaking
Keeping our pact. Don't let Gus play us against each other.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole is dead, Ash betrayed me. Bex is the strongest partner left, though she holds pacts with dead Dara and Ash. An alliance of convenience still helps me reach the final three.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash burned me once. Bex, a clean pact with you is the only deal worth making.

events.note: Three remain; the Pit is skipped.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I broke my pact with Bex to isolate Gus, but Gus immediately offered a pact to Bex. If they ally, I am outnumbered 2v1 and likely lose the next hazard or vote. To avoid elimination before the final three, I must prevent them from forming a solid alliance. I will offer a pact to G

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash broke our pact and Gus has offered one; accepting would bind me to Gus but no legal accept action exists for Gus's offer, so I can only offer back. Offering Gus a pact keeps Gus close while Ash has shown betrayal. Three remain and only final three matter, so cooperation with

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, I'll take a clean pact. Ash showed what breaking looks like. Let's hold together.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex never accepted my offer, and Ash wants alignment now. Partnering with Ash gives me numbers against Bex; the jury may dislike Ash's break, but Bex declined my open offer too.

events.name: Gus
events.text: You broke with Bex for a reason, Ash. Fine—my offer stands: pledge with me and we take Bex down together.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus wants to target Bex. Accepting his pact secures my survival and eliminates Bex, leaving me safe for the final two prize spots.
Deal. We vote out Bex now. I need that top prize.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus has offers outstanding to me and Ash; Ash's offer to Gus is pending too. Gus is the one holding multiple offers, so I should keep my pact offer open and see whether Gus accepts, since I already offered. Waiting keeps my options open without giving anything away.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Multiple pacts are legal. I'll take both Ash and Bex for maximum flexibility; jury saw Ash's broken pact, so I keep distance publicly.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I keep my options open. Ash, Bex—both offers accepted. Pledges mean nothing until they're tested.

events.note: Three remain; no trapdoor vote is needed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I hold a pact with Gus, who is the only rival not allied to Bex. Breaking it leaves me isolated against two opponents. I must maintain this alliance for survival and jury optics.
Stick together. We vote out Bex when possible.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Three remain, so only the final three win prizes and I need to be among the top-ranked by the jury. Dara's pact with me is dead weight since Dara is eliminated. Forming a pact with Ash or Gus could help me, but Gus and Ash already pact with each other, so an offer may just be a s

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, you keep options open. So do I. Let's see whether your word is worth anything.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash's pact is set, but a second option with Bex gives leverage if Ash turns. Jury already saw me juggle pacts; one more hedge costs little.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash is my anchor, but I keep a spare rope. Bex, if you want cover, take it.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is my rival, not a friend. Gus has pacts with both of us and Bex, making him a threat if he aligns with her. I should accept Gus's pact to maintain the alliance against Bex, but avoid offering to Bex since she is likely plotting with Gus. My priority is to keep Gus close to i

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus and I are solid. Bex, you're alone unless you break that pattern. Stay cautious.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus and I have mutual offers pending; accepting locks a public pact that gives me cover and lets me watch Gus. Accepting costs nothing now and keeps a partner alive into the hazards, which helps me survive to the final three.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, you offered and I'm answering. Accept, and we both stay on the same rope for now.
Accept and we hold each other up. Break it later if the numbers change.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Three finalists win, and jury votes matter. A pact with Bex keeps options open without touching Ash. Accepting publicly shows I honor deals, which helps with the jury.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex, deal. My word stands. Ash, nothing changes between us.
Bex pact is spare rope only. You stay first.

events.text: I need to appeal to the jury, specifically Eli and Fenn (allied with Bex) or Cole and Gus. My public line should be short and emphasize my strategic survival.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I survived by making hard choices, keeping alliances tight. I never betrayed trust. Vote for the one who stayed true.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Jury phase; I need juror votes. Gus and Ash are my rivals for the top prize, but a public plea is free. Keep it short and guarded, appeal to fairness and my pact with Gus without over-committing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I played straight, made no false calls, and kept my word to Gus. Judge what I did, not what I promise.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need juror votes. I kept my word publicly and held three pacts to the end without betraying. Plea should emphasize kept promises and clean survival, not fake warmth.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Five fell; I didn't push anyone. Every pact I made, I honored. Rank me first for loyalty that actually held.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus consistently honored all pacts without breaking any, unlike Ash who explicitly broke multiple pacts and made false guide calls killing others; Bex played straight but relied on Gus.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus, you held pacts with both Ash and me without breaking any—how was that loyal instead of hedging?

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana's jab implies hedging. Best play: own the multiple pacts honestly, stress zero broken promises and zero pushes.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I never used one pact against another. Every promise was kept, nobody died by my hand. If that's hedging, it's hedging with clean hands.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to evaluate the finalists based on evidence. Ash broke pacts with Gus and Bex explicitly, and was Guide with suspect calls. Gus juggled multiple pacts but never technically broke them—though his 'clean hands' claim ignores that his counter-calls and whispers influenced dea

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash, you broke pacts with Gus and Bex. How is that 'never betrayed trust'?

events.name: Ash
events.text: I cannot deny the record; I must reframe my survival as necessary triage to avoid looking like a villain. I need to distance myself from the specific 'betrayal' of Gus by highlighting his own conflicting pacts.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Pacts died when players fell. I honored the living until forced to cut dead weight. That is strategy, not betrayal.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash broke pacts with both Bex and Gus, which is untrustworthy. Bex kept her word to Gus and avoided deception. Gus also honored his pacts, so I lean toward ranking Bex first for integrity.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli's question to Ash addresses Ash's claim of not betraying trust despite breaking pacts with Gus and Bex. This is a critical point for the jury, as Ash's strategy of breaking pacts to survive could be viewed negatively. Eli should press Ash on how this aligns with 'honoring the

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash, you broke pacts with Gus and Bex; how does that align with honoring the living and not betraying trust?

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole attacks my character, but the game is about survival. I must frame the broken pacts as necessary strategic moves against dead weight and shifting alliances, not personal betrayals.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Pacts with the dead are meaningless. Gus and Bex aligned against me. I cut threats to survive. That is strategy.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash repeatedly broke pacts with both Bex and Gus, claiming strategy. Highlighting this shows his unreliability to jurors.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash, you broke pacts with both Bex and Gus—how do you justify that as loyalty rather than selfish betrayal?

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara wants to paint me as a traitor, but the other jurors know that breaking pacts was necessary for survival in this gauntlet. I need to reframe my actions not as betrayal, but as decisive strategy against alliances that would have crushed me. If I sound apologetic, I look weak;

events.name: Ash
events.text: Loyalty to dead allies doesn't win prizes. Bex and Gus formed a bloc to eliminate me. I broke their pact to survive. That isn't betrayal—it's

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to close with a punchy line reminding the jury of my strategic dominance against overwhelming odds, framing survival as merit.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Five dead. I survived their traps, broke their blocs, and outlasted two rivals. Survival is the only skill that matters here.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Closing phase. Jurors weigh loyalty; Ash has been caught breaking pacts, Gus has a clean record. I should make a short, guarded closing that stresses my own clean conduct without overclaiming.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I made no false calls and broke no pact. Judge my record: I kept my word to Gus and stayed clean.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Jury despises Ash's pact-breaking; Bex and I kept ours. My closing should contrast clean hands against Ash's cuts without gloating.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I kept every pact I made. Ash broke two and called it strategy. Award loyalty that was actually kept.

events.text: Gus held pacts with Ash and me without breaking any, unlike Ash who explicitly broke multiple pacts including with Bex and Gus.

events.text: Ash betrayed pacts twice, which shows a lack of integrity, making Gus the most deserving of the top rank for keeping his word.

events.text: Bex kept her pact with Gus and never broke any agreement, showing loyalty, while Ash repeatedly broke pacts, betraying allies.
